title: Chamier: formally civil even when the cause is supernatural glory
source_text: XV. Paulo aliter vero ea de re philosophatur Daniel Chamierus. Nam observat civilem cultum dupliciter intelligi posse: vel formaliter, vel causaliter. Civilis cultus formaliter ipsi est, ille qui in se revera civilis est, & distinctus, imo separatus a religioso. Civilis cultus causaliter, quicunque tandem in seipso sit, est tamen a causis mere civilibus. Cum alioqui cultus formaliter civilis possit esse a causis non civilibus, sed supernaturalibus. Et talis est, ex ejus mente, honor qui Sanctis cum Christo regnantibus debetur. Quamvis enim eorum dignitas sit supernaturalis, ideoque cultus qui illis debetur non sit causaliter civilis, est tamen omnino distinctus a cultu Religioso, ac proinde formaliter civilis: nisi quis malit eum officiosum dicere. Panstratia tom. 2. lib. 19. cap. 5. num. 2. & 3.
pass_a_gloss: Daniel Chamier philosophizes a little differently on this matter. For he observes that civil cult can be understood in two ways: either formally or causally. Civil cult formally, for him, is that which in itself is really civil, and distinct, indeed separate, from the religious. Civil cult causally, whatever it finally is in itself, is nevertheless from merely civil causes. Whereas a cult that is formally civil can be from causes that are not civil but supernatural. And such, in his mind, is the honor owed to the Saints reigning with Christ. For although their dignity is supernatural, and therefore the cult owed to them is not causally civil, it is nevertheless wholly distinct from the religious cult, and hence formally civil: unless one prefers to call it dutiful. Panstratia, volume 2, book 19, chapter 5, numbers 2 and 3.
pass_b_english: Chamier splits civil cult into what it is in itself and what causes it.
A cult can be formally civil even when its cause is supernatural.
Honor of the Saints reigning with Christ is of that sort: not causally civil, because their dignity is supernatural, yet wholly distinct from religious cult, and so formally civil.
He allows the alternative name officiosus, dutiful.

choices.why: Chamier's optional name for the same formally civil honor.
